summary: POC scoping call to define latency/throughput SLOs for Novacore conversational assistant. Agreed measurement plan: run controlled benchmarks (synthetic + representative prompts) across hosted and dedicated configs, measure TTFT (time to first token) and TPOT (time per token) at target QPS and concurrency, collect p95/p99 and resource metrics. Next steps: share harness, confirm dataset, schedule baseline run next week.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Novacore CTO), Liam O'Connor (Novacore SRE), Sofia Marin (Novacore ML)
Links shared: Redwood benchmark harness (link), Novacore prompt spreadsheet (TBD)

[00:00:05] Alyssa: okay, hey everyone thanks for carving out time. quick intros, we are here to scope the POC specifically around latency and throughput SLOs — TTFT vs TPOT, and how we'll measure them.
[00:00:23] Priya: thanks Alyssa. priority for us is a snappy user experience for the assistant. we get a lot of pushback when the first token takes too long, and for longer completions the per-token speed really matters.
[00:00:38] Marco: totally, so we usually split goals into TTFT (time to first token) and TPOT (time per token) — TTFT drives perceived latency, TPOT drives throughput and cost.
[00:00:50] Liam: quick question — we run peak at 120 qps right now on our current system, but that's bursty. we care about 99th latency under burst and 95th for steady-state.
[00:01:05] Sofia: our prompts vary: 40% short (10-30 tokens), 40% medium (30-120 tokens), 20% long (120-600 tokens). we'll share a spreadsheet.
[00:01:18] Alyssa: perfect. for scope, recommended initial SLO targets to test against: TTFT p95 <= 250ms, TTFT p99 <= 500ms. TPOT p95 <= 60ms/token, TPOT p99 <= 120ms/token — these are starting points and we'll calibrate to your model size and hosting option.
[00:01:42] Priya: those numbers seem aggressive but plausible — what hardware assumptions?
[00:01:50] Marco: those targets assume a warmed KV cache, optimized kernels, and a dedicated A100/V100-equivalent instance or Redwood Dedicated pool. Hosted variants may be higher until we tune batching. also model variant matters — smaller quantized models will hit TPOT easily.
[00:02:06] Liam: we will likely test with two model flavours: our tuned 7B and a 13B baseline. can we test both?
[00:02:12] Alyssa: yes. recommended plan: run the same scenarios on (1) Redwood Hosted (curated model variants), (2) Redwood Dedicated with tuned quantization, and (3) optional private deployment if you want on-prem metrics.
[00:02:27] Marco: measurement plan detail — we run controlled benchmark runs with loadgen that records per-request TTFT, per-token timing, and token counts. measure p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and TPOT; also capture GPU util, memory, NVLINK, CPU, and network.
[00:02:45] Priya: how do you define TPOT practically? I want to make sure we're not conflating model generation time vs network overhead.
[00:02:52] Marco: good point. TPOT will be measured as (total server-side generation time after first token) / number of generated tokens, so we isolate server-side generation. TTFT includes network send + model first-token compute. we'll run with pinned clients in same region to minimize network noise and also run a local/emulated network test for worst-case.
[00:03:20] Alyssa: we'll also include cold-start vs warm-start scenarios. cold starts measure container spin-up; warm-starts assume kept workers and warmed KV cache. most production SLOs target warmed cases but we log cold metrics for SLA planning.
[00:03:36] Priya: our SLO requirement to the product team is TTFT p95 < 300ms during normal traffic and p99 < 600ms during peak. can we map your proposed numbers to those?
[00:03:47] Marco: yes, we'll produce a mapping matrix: baseline hardware + model -> expected TTFT and TPOT ranges. we will run both short- and long-prompt mixes at target QPS and present p95/p99.
[00:04:02] Liam: about load profile — peak bursts of ~120 qps lasting 2-5 minutes, sustained 25 qps during business hours. we also see a lot of concurrent sessions with streaming responses.
[00:04:16] Sofia: streaming matters — we need the first token fast and steady subsequent token stream. how do you measure streaming latency?
[00:04:24] Marco: streaming is measured as first token arrival time (TTFT) and inter-token gaps; we treat TPOT as average inter-token gap during generation. we'll collect per-token timestamps and report p95/p99 of inter-token gap too.
[00:04:41] Alyssa: for benchmark scenarios we'll define 4 test cases: (A) short prompt burst test at 120 qps, (B) mixed steady-state at 25 qps for 20m, (C) long-prompt throughput at target concurrency 40 concurrent sessions, (D) cold-start churn test with new containers every X minutes to measure cold latency.
[00:05:02] Priya: that covers our main concerns. what about client-side batching and Redwood batching? we already do some request coalescing upstream.
[00:05:10] Marco: we'll test with and without client coalescing. Redwood has continuous batching at the runtime; we can configure max batch size and latency tradeoffs. part of the POC is tuning batch windows to balance TTFT and throughput.
[00:05:26] Liam: how long does a representative run take?
[00:05:29] Alyssa: initial baseline runs are 10-30 minutes per scenario, longer for steady-state to smooth tails. we'll do multiple runs (3+) and aggregate. expect 1 week for baseline collection and initial analysis.
[00:05:42] Priya: ok. what telemetry do you need from our side?
[00:05:45] Marco: ideally: prompt set, expected token distribution, target QPS profile and burst behavior, any region constraints, and representative user sessions for streaming. also access to logs or a synthetic endpoint for the harness to drive.
[00:05:58] Sofia: what about security/compliance? we need SOC 2 and KMS detail before Dedicated testing.
[00:06:05] Alyssa: we'll share security pack and SOC 2 summary. Dedicated and Private options support customer-managed KMS, VPC peering, and audit logs. we'll include those docs in the follow-up.
[00:06:15] Priya: about success criteria — product wants a go/no-go checklist. can you propose concrete pass/fail gates?
[00:06:22] Marco: yes. proposed pass criteria for POC: (1) TTFT p95 <= 300ms and p99 <= 600ms for short/medium prompts under sustained load; (2) TPOT p95 <= 80ms/token and p99 <= 160ms/token for medium-long prompts; (3) System able to handle 120 qps burst with graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model or queued requests) and <2% error rate; (4) Observability: traces and token-level metrics captured for investigation. failures require documented mitigation (batch tuning, smaller model, add capacity).
[00:07:00] Priya: those look reasonable. we might tighten TPOT if cost allows.
[00:07:05] Alyssa: measurement methodology notes — we'll run each scenario 3x at different times of day, collect raw per-request logs (ttft_ms, total_tokens, total_generation_ms), compute per-request tpot_ms = total_generation_ms / total_tokens, and then aggregate p50/p95/p99 across requests. we will also log GPU metrics with 1s granularity to correlate tails to GC/compaction/eviction events.
[00:07:31] Liam: do you simulate KV cache warm states? we have lots of prefix reuse.
[00:07:35] Marco: yes, we will have a warm-up stage where we run representative traffic for 10-15 minutes to populate prefix/KV caches before the actual measurement window. we'll also capture cold-window baselines.
[00:07:49] Sofia: what about tokenization differences and prompt formatting? small changes can move token counts a lot.
[00:07:54] Alyssa: good call — we'll canonicalize prompts with your tokenizer and record token counts used in the metrics. please provide tokenization script or we can run one with your model.
[00:08:06] Priya: timeline summary?
[00:08:09] Alyssa: week 0 (this week): share harness + runbook, customer shares dataset and traffic profile; week 1: baseline runs on hosted + dedicated, initial analysis; week 2: tuning (batch/window/quantization), run longer steady-state; week 3: final report and go/no-go review. so about 2-3 weeks end-to-end for an initial POC.
[00:08:34] Marco: also note we should include cost per 1M tokens estimates for each config to help product decide tradeoffs.
[00:08:41] Priya: yes, please.
[00:08:43] Alyssa: open items: (1) Priya to upload prompt set & tokenization script, (2) Alyssa to send harness link + quickstart, (3) Marco to draft initial SLO matrix for both models and hosting modes.
[00:08:57] Liam: one more operational ask — can you simulate partial region outage? we need to know failover latency to backup region.
[00:09:06] Marco: we can simulate region routing failures and measure failover times and fallbacks; that will be an optional scenario in the POC.
[00:09:14] Sofia: any gotchas we should expect?
[00:09:17] Marco: common gotchas: batching windows causing TTFT spikes, KV cache thrash if working set larger than cache, and network egress spikes if embeddings/ops run concurrently. we'll instrument these.
[00:09:30] Priya: great. thanks. who will own the final report?
[00:09:33] Alyssa: Redwood will produce the final POC report (metrics, configs, recommendations) and Novacore will validate against product acceptance criteria.
[00:09:42] Priya: sounds good.
[00:09:44] Alyssa: okay let's recap and call out next steps.
[00:09:48] Marco: recap: share harness, confirm dataset/traffic, schedule baseline run, produce SLO proposal, run tests across hosted/dedicated, deliver report in ~2 weeks.
[00:09:59] Priya: thanks everyone. we'll aim to have the prompt set by Friday.
[00:10:03] Alyssa: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and the schedule.

[00:10:15] NOTE: transcription includes occasional mis-hears and product name variations (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" vs "Redwood Dedicated").
